title: Land Cruiser 70 Series
verdict: The 70 is the Land Cruiser Toyota forgot to stop building, and nobody who needs one has ever complained. Leaf springs, a part-time transfer case, manual hubs and a cabin with all the sound deadening of a grain silo: it is a farm tool that happens to cross continents.
codes: NEVER SOLD NEW IN THE US

paragraphs: The 70 Series arrived in 1984 to replace the 25-year-old [[land-cruiser/fj40|40 Series]] as the Land Cruiser that does the hard work, while the [[land-cruiser/fj60|60 Series]] wagon line drifted toward comfort and, eventually, the [[land-cruiser/80-series|80 Series]]. More than four decades later it is still in production. It has been built in Japan, Portugal, Venezuela and Colombia, and it has served as a troop carrier, a mine truck and a military patrol vehicle. What it has never been is a new car you can buy at an American Toyota dealer.

story.heading: A 40 SERIES IN A SQUARER SUIT
paragraphs: The styling kept a family resemblance to the 40 but went more angular, and the range came in every length a farmer could want. Wikipedia's breakdown is the one owners use: 70 and 71 were the short wheelbase, 73 and 74 the medium, 75 and later 78 and 79 the long-wheelbase pickups and troop carriers, and 76 and 77 the semi-long four-door wagons. The letters in front give the engine away, so an FJ70 has the 3F petrol six, an HJ75 the 2H diesel, and an HZJ75 the 1HZ.

There were lighter-duty 70s as well, sold as the Bundera, the Land Cruiser II and eventually the Prado. That branch grew softer with each update, and by 1997 the Prado had become the 90 Series with no real connection to the workhorse. Some markets got odd variants, too: Portugal, Spain and Italy received a BJ73 with a VM Motori five-cylinder turbo-diesel, built by Salvador Caetano in Portugal.

story.heading: LEAVES, COILS AND A V8
paragraphs: The big mechanical change came with the August 1999 facelift. The front axle moved from leaf springs to coils with leading arms, the rear leaves got longer for more articulation and a better ride, wheels went from six studs to five, and the long-wheelbase models were renamed 78 (troop carrier) and 79 (pickup). The short-wheelbase truck disappeared from most markets, and Japanese sales ended in June 2004 because the truck couldn't meet Japan's NOx and particulate rules.

In 2007 Toyota fitted the 4.5-liter 1VD-FTV turbo-diesel V8. It needed a wider chassis, a wider front axle and a new nose that finally did away with the flat fenders every commercial Land Cruiser had worn since the 40. The four-door 76 wagon was added to the range, and a dressed-up GXL trim arrived. Petrol 70s swapped the 1FZ six for the 1GR-FE V6 in 2009, and a double-cab 79 with a 130-liter tank followed in 2012.

story.heading: THE TRUCK THAT WON'T RETIRE
paragraphs: In Australia, where the 70 is part of the furniture, the V8 picked up a diesel particulate filter and piezo injectors in late 2016 to meet Euro 5. The same update gave the single-cab ute curtain and driver's-knee airbags and a thicker, stronger chassis, which earned it five ANCAP stars. In 2023 came a 2.8-liter four-cylinder turbo-diesel with a six-speed automatic, LED headlights and a 40 Series-style gauge cluster. Japan, which had already given the 70 a one-year 30th-anniversary run in 2014–15, put it back on sale in November 2023.

The V8 didn't survive. Toyota Australia ended production of the V8 wagon and troop carrier in September 2024, citing 'changing regulations and community expectations,' and kept only the GXL pickups going into 2025. The four-cylinder makes 201 hp and 369 lb-ft (500 Nm) with the automatic, and from October 2024 it was also offered with a five-speed manual, detuned to 332 lb-ft. Unsealed 4X4's verdict is that plenty of enthusiasts still prefer the pre-DPF 2007–2016 V8s, mainly because they're mechanically simpler.

story.heading: HOW AN AMERICAN GETS ONE
paragraphs: Toyota never offered the 70 in the United States. Canada got a few BJ70s for the 1985–87 model years with the 3B and 13B-T diesels, and as of 2022 Canadian mines could still buy them through Toyota Industrial Sales Canada. For everyone else in North America, the route is the gray market. Since 1989 NHTSA has exempted vehicles more than 25 years old from the rules it administers, so each year a new batch of older 70s becomes legal to import.

That's why the IH8MUD 70-Series Tech forum is full of American owners with BJ74s, HJ75s and 1HZ troopies, and why the 80 Series and the 70 often share a driveway. If you want the 80's toughness without the 80's comfort, the 70 is the purer version. It also makes the [[land-cruiser/100-series|100 Series]] and [[land-cruiser/200-series|200 Series]] look positively soft.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE 70 GOES TO WAR
callout.title: The Al-Thalab and other militarized 79s
paragraphs: The same qualities that make the 79 a good station truck — a heavy-duty chassis, simple mechanicals that can be fixed in the field and little reliance on electronics — made it the base for a long-range patrol vehicle. In 2000 the UK firm Jankel, working with Jordan's King Abdullah Design and Development Bureau, started designing the Al-Thalab on the Land Cruiser 79 chassis.

In base form it carries up to four crew and 1,700 kg of equipment, with three firing positions and two radio stations. Jordan's army ordered it in 2004 and now runs more than 200, Mauritania has used it since 2006, and British special forces were seen in Al-Thalabs in Syria in 2016. More recently, Babcock built its GLV on the 79 chassis and France's Technamm Masstech T4 used the HZJ76.

engineering_intro: Under the boxy body is a heavy-duty ladder frame, in more wheelbases than any other Land Cruiser line, with live axles at both ends. Every heavy-duty 70 has a leaf-sprung rear axle. The front ran on leaf springs until 1999 and on coils with leading arms after that. Drive goes through a part-time transfer case with high and low range and manual locking hubs, and Toyota offered selectable front and rear lockers in some markets.

engineering.note: 2,310 mm short-wheelbase up to the 3,180 mm 79 pickup. The 2007 frame got wider to fit the V8.

engineering.v: Live axle: leaf springs, then coils from 1999
engineering.note: The 1999 facelift brought coil springs with leading arms and a slightly lighter front axle.
On every heavy-duty 70. Rear leaves were lengthened in 1999 for more articulation and a softer ride.
Manual locking hubs on a full-floating front axle. Rear axles came in semi- and full-floating versions.
Factory options in some markets. ARB and Harrop are the usual aftermarket routes.
DPF added from late 2016. The last V8s were GXL utes delivered in late 2025. Elsewhere: the 1HZ diesel six, the 1GR-FE V6 and, from 2023, the 2.8 L 1GD-FTV four.

generations_table.engine: 3B / 13B-T diesel I4 · 3F petrol I6 · 2H diesel I6
generations_table.note: Original leaf-sprung trucks. Canada got a few BJ70s (MY 1985–87).

generations_table.engine: 1HZ 4.2 diesel I6 · 1PZ 3.4 diesel I5 · 1FZ 4.5 petrol I6 (from 1992)
generations_table.note: The 1HZ became the default workhorse engine and is still offered in some markets.
Second facelift: coil-sprung front axle, five-stud wheels, 78 troopy and 79 pickup names.
Wider front track and frame, 76 wagon added, DPF from late 2016. V8 wagon and troopy production ended September 2024; GXL utes ran into late 2025.
Replaced the 1FZ in petrol markets such as the Middle East, Bolivia and Colombia.
First six-speed automatic in a 70, plus a five-speed manual in Australia from October 2024. Back on sale in Japan from late 2023.

buying_checks.head: Check the A-pillars for rust
buying_checks.body: Unsealed 4X4 says rust usually starts from the inside, so look for bubbling and flaking paint and run a magnet over suspect areas. Coastal trucks rot in the A-pillars and let water in. The magazine knows of one owner who paid nearly A$15,000 to replace both pillars, so its advice is to walk away.

buying_checks.head: Look at the rear spring hangers
buying_checks.body: Trucks that regularly ran over GVM on rough roads can crack at the weld where the rear spring hanger meets the frame. Look for cracks, fresh welds or reinforcement plates, and listen for a clunk under load.

buying_checks.head: Open the airbox
buying_checks.body: On the V8, a weak airbox seal lets dust past the filter. Unclip the lid and check the clean side of the filter: if there's dust there, Unsealed says the engine is on borrowed time.

buying_checks.head: Shift through every gear
buying_checks.body: Crunching between second and third points to worn synchros. Unsealed 4X4 blames GL-5 oil, whose extreme-pressure additives attack the yellow-metal synchro rings, and says to use GL-4 75W-90. Other spec sheets list GL-4 or GL-5, so check what your manual calls for.

buying_checks.head: Test the clutch on tuned trucks
buying_checks.body: The stock clutch is built for stock power. If the revs rise without the truck accelerating, or it bites at the very top of the pedal, budget for a heavy-duty clutch.

buying_checks.head: Jack up the front wheels
buying_checks.body: Grab each front tire at 12 and 6 o'clock and rock it. Play or a hum that rises to a howl with speed points to front wheel bearings, which work hard on heavy, big-tired 70s.

buying_checks.head: Ask about the DPF (late-2016-on V8s)
buying_checks.body: Look for DPF warning lights, smoke or a history of limp mode, especially on trucks that mostly did short trips.

buying_checks.head: Importing? Check the build date
buying_checks.body: For a US import, NHTSA's exemption is based on age: the truck must be more than 25 years old. Check the build plate before you pay, and remember that a lot of imports have spent their lives working on farms or mine sites.

repairs.title: Adjust or replace the front wheel bearings
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day for both sides
repairs.cost: About A$500 a side at a mechanic, per Unsealed 4X4
repairs.symptoms: A hum from the front that becomes a growl, then a howl, and gets louder with speed. With the wheel off the ground, there's play when you rock it at 12 and 6 o'clock.
repairs.fix: The 70 uses the same tapered-roller hub design Toyota has used since the 40 Series. Remove the locking hub, take off the lock nut with a 54 mm socket and tighten the bearing back up. Sometimes that and fresh grease are all it needs. If the bearings are worn, replace them. Many owners service the swivel hubs at the same time, since they need doing periodically anyway.
repairs.tools: 54 mm hub socket · torque wrench · bearing grease · new tapered roller bearings and seals if replacing.

parts.name: Front wheel bearing kit (Koyo), 1998–2019 solid-axle non-US 7x (FAWB9819SAK)
Front axle rebuild kit, 8/1999–2019 7x non-ABS (FA9919)
Front axle rebuild kit, 8/2012+ 7x with ABS (FA1219)

repairs.title: Stop dust getting past the airbox (1VD V8)
repairs.cost: Free to check; an aftermarket airbox costs more
repairs.symptoms: Red dust on the clean side of the filter, MAF sensor faults, limp mode in the middle of a dusty trip, or a noisy turbo.
repairs.fix: Unclip the airbox lid and inspect the downstream side of the filter. Some mechanics grease the factory seal and some owners make their own seals from silicone and D-rubber, but Unsealed's preferred fix is an aftermarket airbox that seals the intake properly. If you find dust, clean the MAF sensor and check the turbo for shaft play.
repairs.tools: Screwdriver · torch · MAF cleaner · replacement seal or aftermarket airbox.

parts.name: Scavenger air filter, VDJ 70 Series
Scavenger snorkel, V8 VDJ facelift 70 Series

repairs.title: Fit proper bulb-type door seals
repairs.cost: A couple of hundred dollars for a four-door 76, per Unsealed
repairs.symptoms: Wind noise that gets worse with age, whistling at town speeds, diesel fumes in traffic, and a dusty dash after a day on dirt roads.
repairs.fix: The factory flat pinch-weld seals never fully close the gap. Pull them and fit bulb-type seals that compress when the door shuts. Unsealed notes the door openings have stayed the same since 1985, so the same seals fit every 70.
repairs.tools: Trim tool · bulb-type door seal kit · adhesive if the kit calls for it.

parts.name: OEM front door weatherstrip, RH hardtop, 7x (WS60030R) — factory part, not the bulb upgrade

repairs.title: Refill the manual gearbox with the right oil
repairs.symptoms: Crunching shifts, especially between second and third.
repairs.fix: Drain the gearbox and refill with GL-4 75W-90, which is what Unsealed specifies for the V8 trucks (confirm the grade in your manual, since some spec sheets allow GL-4 or GL-5). Unsealed warns that the extreme-pressure additives in GL-5 attack the yellow metal in the synchros. Pause briefly mid-shift and avoid forcing shifts when the box is cold. If it still crunches, plan a rebuild before the gear teeth get damaged, and do the clutch at the same time.
repairs.tools: Drain and fill plug wrenches · fluid pump · GL-4 75W-90 gear oil.

parts.name: Red Line MT-90 75W-90 GL-4 gear oil

repairs.title: Repair a cracked rear spring hanger
repairs.symptoms: A clunk from the rear under heavy load, such as towing up a hill, and a wandering feel in corners if the crack has grown.
repairs.fix: Unsealed's order: have the crack professionally welded, add chassis bracing straight away from someone who's very good with a MIG, then fit the GVM upgrade the truck should have had in the first place. After that, check the area at every service.
repairs.tools: Welder and grinder (or a fab shop) · bracing plates · GVM-rated springs.

parts.name: OME greaseable spring pin kit, 78/79 rear (OME GP7) — refresh while the hanger is apart

repairs.title: Upgrade the clutch on a tuned V8
repairs.cost: Parts plus labor; tuning shops often bundle a tune with a clutch
repairs.symptoms: Revs climb while acceleration stays the same or drops off, the clutch bites only near the top of the pedal, and shifts start grinding.
repairs.fix: Replace the clutch with a heavy-duty unit rated for the torque you're making. If the gearbox is already crunchy, rebuild it while it's out.
repairs.tools: Transmission jack · clutch alignment tool · heavy-duty clutch kit.

parts.name: Exedy clutch finder (heavy-duty kits by model)

repairs.title: Revive or upgrade the alternator
repairs.symptoms: Hard starting, slow charging of auxiliary batteries and charging warnings on the dash.
repairs.fix: The stock 130–150 A alternator sits low and catches mud and dust. Rinse it with a low-pressure hose after every trip. If you've added big lithium systems, Unsealed says to fit a bigger alternator, such as a 240 A Jaylec unit or a sealed one, and to use a proper DC-DC charger.
repairs.tools: Basic hand tools · low-pressure hose · uprated alternator if needed.

parts.name: Jaylec 65-8594EP 130 A corrosion-protected alternator, VDJ
Landcruiser VDJ 220 A alternator

repairs.title: Make the air conditioning work
repairs.symptoms: The cabin never gets cool on a hot day, and the back seat of a 79 dual-cab is miserable.
repairs.fix: Clean the condenser of dust, grass and bugs first. Then consider an AC amplifier such as Freezebrain, which plugs into the factory controller to lower the evaporator temperature and can add idle-up control.
repairs.tools: Soft brush and hose · plug-in AC controller.

parts.name: FreezeBrain LC70 AC amplifier (88650-60G20 replacement)
Genuine Denso TX valve, LC70 VDJ

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: The IH8MUD consensus for a stock-height long-wheelbase 70 is 235/85R16, about 31.7 inches. 285/75R16 (33 inches) will go on, but on factory steel wheels owners report it rubs on the inside at full lock unless you change wheel offset. Short-wheelbase owners in the same thread treat 255/85R16 (about 33 inches) as the sensible upper limit, and the one running them has a lift. Sagging old springs make everything rub sooner.

faq.q: Can I buy one in the US?
faq.a: Not new. Toyota never sold the 70 in the United States. Canada got a few BJ70s for the 1985–87 model years and, as of 2022, Canadian mining companies could still buy them. Americans import older trucks under the rule NHTSA set in 1989 exempting vehicles more than 25 years old.

Body and wheelbase. Since 1999, 78 is the long-wheelbase troop carrier and 79 the long-wheelbase pickup (single and, from 2012, dual cab); the 76 is the four-door wagon. Earlier, 70/71 were short wheelbase, 73/74 medium, 75 long, and 77 a semi-long wagon.

faq.q: Which years and engines are best?
faq.a: Unsealed 4X4 says many enthusiasts prefer the 2007–2016 V8s, which don't have a DPF, but that service history matters more than the year. For US imports, the age rule means older trucks, typically with the 1HZ, 2H, 3B or 13B-T diesels or the 3F and 1FZ petrol sixes.
Selectable front and rear lockers were factory options in some markets. Otherwise ARB Air Lockers and Harrop electric lockers are the common add-ons; one IH8MUD owner runs Harrop E-lockers in a BJ74.

Rarely. Most 70s are manual, but a four-speed auto was offered on a few versions: FJ73 (1985–1992), BJ74, HZJ73/77 (1990–1999) and HZJ74/76K (1999–2004). The 2.8 L four that arrived in 2023 came with a six-speed automatic.
Australian V8s got a diesel particulate filter from September 2016 to meet Euro 5. Earlier V8s don't have one. Unsealed recommends a good highway run every 1,000–2,000 km to let it regenerate.

faq.q: Why are the rear wheels inboard of the fronts on V8 trucks?
faq.a: To make room for the 1VD-FTV, Toyota fitted a wider front axle and frame in 2007, which left the front and rear tracks different. Superior Engineering's coil conversion is one of the aftermarket fixes Unsealed mentions for equalizing them.

In Australia, yes. V8 wagon and troop carrier production ended in September 2024, and the GXL pickups were the last V8s, shipping until late 2025. The 2.8 L four replaced it: 201 hp and 369 lb-ft with the six-speed automatic, or 332 lb-ft with the five-speed manual added in October 2024.

Overall, yes, says Unsealed: a strong engine and a tough driveline, with many trucks running very high mileage. The known weak points are mostly about use and comfort: DPFs on late V8s, clutches on tuned trucks, gearbox synchros, front wheel bearings, dust past the airbox, leaky door seals, weak AC and frame cracks on overloaded pickups.

faq.q: Leaf springs or coils up front?
faq.a: Leaf springs up to the 1999 facelift, then coils with leading arms. The rear stayed on leaf springs.

mods.why: Many 70s are either overloaded or riding on springs rated for loads they never carry. Matching the springs to the real load, or fitting a GVM upgrade, fixes ride and safety. A coil conversion is the expensive way to fix both ride and track width at once.
Factory lockers were only offered in some markets. Selectable air or electric lockers turn an open-diff 70 into a proper rock truck.
Unsealed's fix for the cabin: thicker seat covers (Black Duck's add about 20 mm of padding), or full replacement seats, plus sound-deadening mats.
A winch bumper up front and a swing-out at the back are the standard build for a working or touring 70.

who.name: Cruiser Outfitters — 70 Series dual swing-out rear bumper

mods.why: Raises the intake for water crossings and dusty roads, and pairs well with a properly sealed airbox on the V8.
For imported trucks in North America, specialist Land Cruiser parts houses are the easiest route to genuine and OEM-supplier parts.

baseline_service.intro: Most 70s in the US are 25-year-old grey imports (1HZ, 1PZ, 1HD-FTE or petrol 3F/1FZ), while newer markets got the 1VD-FTV V8, so first confirm the exact model code and engine on the VIN plate. Specs below are given for the 4.5 V8 (VDJ79, Roughtrax) and the 1HZ (Toyota publications via IH8MUD); anything else, check the manual. Unsealed's rule applies to all of them: service history beats odometer.

items.note: On post-2016 DPF trucks a low-ash C-spec oil matters; don't fill one with old-school high-ash diesel oil.
